The choice of the sound masculine plural (jam' al-salim) is by way of giving precedence to the males over the females. This indicates that the Governor (al-'Aziz) was a forbearing man, since he was content to hold her accountable only to this degree.

Ibn Kathir said: "Or he excused her, because she had seen what she could not patiently bear. It is also said that he was little given to jealousy."

Al-Shihab said: "And this is a kindness from God, exalted is He, toward Joseph, peace be upon him."

Abu Hayyan said: "It is what the soil of Egypt requires." End of quotation.

It has been established among the scholars of verification that the differing conditions of civilization, in fertility and drought, and its climates, in heat and cold and what follows from them, have an effect on the characters and bodies of people. See the Fourth and Fifth Introductions in (The Muqaddimah of Ibn Khaldun).

Then God, exalted is He, mentioned that the story of Joseph and the wife of the Governor spread in the city — and it is Egypt — by His saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[30] ﴿And women in the city said, "The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her young man from himself. He has certainly captivated her heart with love. Indeed, we see her in clear error."﴾

﴿And women in the city said, "The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her young man from himself."﴾ Al-'Aziz: the ruler (al-amir), derived from (al-'izz), which means severity and domination. The term became especially associated with the ruler of Egypt and Alexandria.

﴿He has certainly captivated her heart with love﴾ That is, his love pierced through her (shaghaf), until it reached the heart. Al-shaghaf (the covering of the heart), like sahab (cloud) in its pattern, is the membrane enclosing the heart.

(p-3535) ﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾ That is, in mistake, straying from the path of rectitude and correctness. The insertion of "seeing" (ru'yah) indicates that their judgment of her being in error proceeds from sight and knowledge, while also hinting at their own freedom from such conduct.

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[31] ﴿So when she heard of their scheming, she sent to them and prepared for them a banquet, and gave each of them a knife, and said, "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they magnified him, and cut their hands, and said, "Far be Allah from imperfection! This is not a human. This is none other than a noble angel."﴾

﴿When she heard of their scheming﴾ means their backbiting and their evil talk. The word "scheming" (al-makr) is used metaphorically (istiʿara) for "backbiting" (al-ghība) because of their resemblance in concealment. Or "scheming" is used in its literal sense, and they had said this so that she would show them Yusuf.

﴿She sent to them﴾ means she invited them to a meal, scheming against them. ﴿And prepared﴾ means she readied and arranged. ﴿For them a banquet﴾ means what they would recline upon of cushions. ﴿And gave each of them a knife﴾ means so that they would cut with it what they ate of fruits and the like. ﴿And said﴾ means to Yusuf, ﴿"Come out before them"﴾ means appear before them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: By that arrangement, which is their reclining while the knives were in their hands, she intended that they be astonished and stunned upon seeing him, and that they be distracted from themselves, so that their hands would fall upon their own hands and cut them. For when one who is reclining is stunned by something, his hand falls upon his other hand. Thus she would silence them with proof. And that is what happened, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, meaning they exalted him and were overwhelmed by his surpassing beauty. ﴿And cut their hands﴾ means they wounded them, as when you say, "I was cutting the meat and I cut my hand," meaning you wounded it. ﴿And said, "Far be Allah from imperfection! This is not a human. This is none other than a noble angel."﴾ The word "Far be" (ḥāsha) is originally ḥāshā, and its alif was dropped for lightness. Abu ʿAmr read it this way in continuous recitation (al-durj, reading without pause between words). It means glorification of Him, glorified is He, above attributes of deficiency and incapacity, and an expression of wonder at His power to produce such a wondrous creation. They denied humanness of him only because of the strangeness of his beauty, and affirmed for him angelhood, in the manner of restriction (al-qaṣr), based on what is fixed in human nature: that nothing is more beautiful than an angel, just as it is fixed in human nature that nothing is uglier than Satan. For this reason, everything extreme in beauty or ugliness is likened to these two.

(p-3536)

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[32] ﴿She said, "That is the one you blamed me for. I did seek to seduce him, but he remained chaste. And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned, and he will surely be of the humiliated."﴾

﴿She said, "That is the one you blamed me for"﴾ i.e., for being infatuated with him. ﴿I did seek to seduce him, but he remained chaste﴾ i.e., he refused, seeking chastity and asking for more of it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The form isti'sam (istis'am) is an intensive form (bina' mubalagha), indicating a forceful refusal and a strong guarding of oneself, as if he were in a state of protection (ismah), while he strives to seek more of it. Its like is istamsaka (he held fast), istawsa'a al-fatq (the tear widened), istajma'a al-ra'y (he gathered his opinion), and istafhala al-khatb (the matter grew severe). This is an explanation of what came from Yusuf, peace be upon him, which admits of no addition, and a proof, than which nothing is brighter, that he was innocent of what the people of hashw (superfluous, unreliable commentators) attributed to him, of what they interpreted as hamm (desire) and burhan (proof). End of quote.

﴿And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned﴾ i.e., he will surely be punished with prison and confinement; ﴿and he will surely be of the humiliated﴾ i.e., of the abased and disgraced.

When Yusuf heard her threat:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿He said, "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me. And unless You turn their plot away from me, I will incline toward them and be among the ignorant."﴾

﴿He said, "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me"﴾ That is, than complying with them. For it is a small hardship, followed by eternal comforts. Then he sought refuge with God Exalted, asking for protection (al-'ismah), by saying: ﴿And unless You turn their plot away from me﴾, meaning: what they desire from me. ﴿I will incline toward them﴾, that is, I would be inclined to answer them by the demands of human nature. ﴿And be among the ignorant﴾, that is, because of committing what they invite me to of ugliness (al-qabih).

Abu al-Su'ud said: This is a seeking of refuge, peace be upon him, in the subtle kindnesses (alteef) of God Exalted, following the custom of the prophets and the righteous, in confining the attainment of goods and deliverance from evils to the threshold of God, Mighty and Majestic, and in stripping their own selves of power and capacity. And it is an intensification in calling upon His kindness to turn away their plot, by showing that he has no power to repel it, like the words of one who cries for help: "Reach me, or I am lost," not that he was seeking to be compelled and forced into chastity and modesty, while in himself there was an impulse calling him toward their desires. End of quote.

Al-Qashani said: That supplication is the form of the heart's necessary neediness (iftiqar) at all times.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[34] ﴿So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plotting. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

﴿So his Lord responded to him﴾ means: He answered his supplication. ﴿And turned away from him their plotting﴾ means: He strengthened him with a holy strengthening (ta'yid qudsi), turning him toward the sacred presence (janab al-quds), and by this He warded off from him their plotting. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ means: He hears the supplications of those who humbly beseech Him. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾ means: He knows what will set them right.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[35] ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time.﴾

﴿Then it occurred to them﴾, i.e., it became apparent to al-'Azīz and his people; ﴿after they had seen the signs﴾, i.e., the evidences of his innocence; ﴿that they should imprison him for a time﴾, i.e., until a period in which they would see fit to do so.

(p-3538) The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of the deeper meaning) of His saying, may He be exalted:

[36] ﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine," and the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying on my head bread, of which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation. Indeed, we see you to be among the doers of good."﴾

﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men.﴾ It is narrated that they were two slaves of the Pharaoh of Egypt. One of them was the chief of his cupbearers, and the other was the chief of his food. The king was angry with them and imprisoned them, so they were with Yusuf. Then one day he saw them distressed, and he asked them about their condition. They mentioned to him that they had seen a dream that had grieved them, and there was no one to interpret it for them. So he said to them, "Is not interpretation belonging to God? Relate it to me!" This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿One of them said﴾, and he was the one in charge of his drink: ﴿"Indeed, I see myself pressing wine."﴾ That is, grapes, calling the grapes by what they will become. Or, in the dialect of Oman, *khamr* is the name for grapes. He said: "I saw in the dream as if before me was a vessel in which were three clusters of grapes. Then their bunches ripened and became grapes, and Pharaoh's cup was in my hand. So I took the grapes and pressed them into the cup, and I handed it to Pharaoh."

﴿And the other said﴾, and he was the one in charge of his food: ﴿"Indeed, I see myself carrying on my head bread, of which the birds eat."﴾ That is because he said to him: "I saw as if on my head were three baskets of fine white flour (*ḥuwwārā*), and the birds were eating from the uppermost basket on my head."

﴿Inform us of its interpretation﴾, that is, tell us the explanation of what we saw and what this vision will lead to. ﴿Indeed, we see you to be among the doers of good﴾, that is, among those who interpret dreams well, or among those who do good to the people of the prison: you treat their sick, console their sorrowful, and provide generously for their poor. So do good to us by removing our distress, if you are able to do that.

Then he, peace be upon him, indicated to them that what they had seen was easy to interpret, because its likeness exists in the dream, and that he has a knowledge beyond that, which is that he explains to them every great and subtle matter of future affairs, even if there is no preceding cause in the dream. Even the food that is assigned to come to them every day, he explains to them before it comes. This is not from the category of soothsaying (*kahana*), but from the Lord's grace toward whomever He chooses for prophethood. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted:

The discussion of His words, Exalted is He:

[37] ﴿He said, "No food will come to you as provision that you are given except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it reaches you. That is part of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have abandoned the creed of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers."﴾

﴿He said, "No food will come to you as provision that you are given except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it reaches you"﴾ That is, before it reaches you. By "food" is meant what is sent to the people of the prison. Its "interpretation" (ta'wil) is the mention of what it is, by saying: "There will come to you food of such-and-such a kind," and they will find it just as he described. The reality of ta'wil (interpretation, here meaning the explanation of what is meant by words where that meaning differs from their apparent sense) is the explanation of the intended meaning.

Abu al-Su'ud said: His applying the term to specifying what food will come later is either by way of metaphor (isti'ara), since that, in relation to food in general, which is indefinite, is in the position of ta'wil, considering what was seen in the dream, and is similar to it. Or it is by way of mushakala (the figure of speech in which one term is used because of its association with another), in keeping with what occurred in their words: ﴿Inform us of its interpretation﴾ [Yusuf: 36]. His intention, peace be upon him, by this was to explain everything that concerns them of matters awaited before they occur. The food was singled out for mention because it was prominent in that respect given the circumstances, together with what it contains of observing the goodness of the transition (husn al-takhallus) to it from the two dreams they had related, which concerned drink and food.

﴿That﴾ means that interpretation and the reporting of unseen things ﴿is part of what my Lord has taught me﴾, that is, through revelation and inspiration, not from soothsaying (takahhun) or astrology (tanjim). In this there is an indication that he possesses many sciences, of which what the two heard is but a fragment of their jewels. His, Exalted is He, words: ﴿Indeed, I have abandoned the creed of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[38] ﴿And I have followed the religion (millah) of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾

This sentence is either introduced to explain the reason why Allah taught him through revelation and inspiration, meaning that He singled him out for this because he abandoned disbelief and followed the path of his forefathers, the messengers. Or it is a new statement, mentioned as a preface to the call and to show that he comes from the household of prophethood, so that their desire to listen to him and their trust in him would grow. By his abandoning the religion of disbelief is meant that he refrained from it entirely, as his saying reveals: ﴿It was not for us to associate anything with Allah﴾, meaning that it was not valid or proper for us to do that, let alone commit it. He expressed it this way because it is more fitting, by outward reckoning, for his following of his fathers, peace be upon him. The specification of them, although associating partners with Allah is also not valid for anyone else, is because the prohibition for others is established by a more evident means. Or the intended meaning is the negation of its occurrence from them, due to their being protected from sin. The repetition of (they) serves to indicate their exclusivity and to emphasize their disbelief in the Hereafter. The addition of (min) in the object, namely "min shay'" (anything), serves to emphasize generality, meaning that we do not associate with Him any of the things at all, whether little or insignificant, whether an idol, a king, a jinn, or anything else.

His saying: ﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾ means that not associating anything with Allah, which is monotheism (tawhid), is among the general blessings of Allah, for which He must be thanked, since He guided us to it through sound natural disposition (fitrah) and by setting up the evidences within the self and in the horizons.

**(p. 3541)**

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

Then He explained that most people rejected this blessing after it had become incumbent upon them to be grateful for it.

When he, peace be upon him, mentioned the upright religion that he followed, he gently proceeded to argue against the falsehood of what their people worshipped, namely idols. He set forth for them an example by which the truth becomes perfectly clear, saying:

[39] ﴿O my two fellow prisoners! Are many diverse lords better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?﴾

﴿O my two fellow prisoners!﴾ He described them with companionship, which necessarily entails affection and the giving of sincere advice. That is, "O my two companions in it" (*fihi*, "in it"). He made the adverbial complement (*ẓarf*, a noun of time or place functioning as a complement) an object by way of extension. So the meaning is: "Are many diverse lords, who enslave people, better for them, or is there for them one Lord, the Irresistible, who cannot be overcome?"

Some scholars said: The verse indicates that the sharia (divine law), just as it demands belief, also guides to the good in it. This is because this verse clearly points out that the multiplicity of gods divides people in the direction of their hearts toward the greatest authority they take above their own strength. It drives each group to fanaticism toward what its heart has been turned to, and in that is the corruption of their order, as is well known. As for the belief of all of them in one God, it is an affirmation of oneness (*tawhid*) that unifies their souls toward one authority, to whose rule all submit, and in that is the order of their brotherhood, which is the foundation of their happiness. Thus the sharia came explaining the reality that knowledge of God through His attributes is good in itself; it is not the creator of goodness. End of quote.

In His saying, ﴿Are many diverse lords﴾, there is an allusion to what the people of Egypt were upon in his time, peace be upon him, of worshipping various idols.

Some say: Just as Egypt had prevailed in knowledge and power, so too in the worship of idols, for its people surpassed everyone else in misguidance. They used to prostrate to the sun, the moon, the stars, human figures, and animals, even insects and the lowest creeping things of the earth.

(p-3542) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[40] ﴿You worship not, apart from Him, but names which you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the right religion, but most people do not know.﴾

﴿You worship not, apart from Him﴾, that is, apart from Allah, ﴿but names which you have named, you and your fathers﴾. He means: you named things that do not deserve divinity as gods, and then you began to worship them. So it is as if you worship nothing but empty names with no realities beneath them. ﴿For which Allah has sent down no authority﴾, that is, no proof indicating their validity. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾, that is, in the matter of worship and religion, ﴿because He is the Owner, and He has not judged that they be worshipped; for He ﴿has commanded that you worship none but Him﴾, because worship is the utmost humility, and so it is due only to one who has the utmost greatness. ﴿That﴾, that is, the Tawhid that indicates the perfection of Allah's greatness, such that none other shares it with Him, ﴿is the right religion﴾, that is, the upright, true, and enduring truth. ﴿But most people do not know﴾, that is, due to their ignorance. For this reason most of them are polytheists.

A Note:

It is not hidden that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said: No food will come to you﴾ [Yusuf: 37] up to here is an introduction to answering their question about the interpretation of their dream. Upon him be peace, he paved the way with it to invite them to Tawhid, so that they would increase in knowledge of the greatness of his station and in confidence in his affair, seeking by that a means to achieve what he hoped for of guiding them, especially since one of them was about to be overtaken by death through crucifixion, so he hoped that he would end with good.

Al-Zamakhshari said: When they praised him and described him as one who does good, he took that as a reason to mention a description of himself that exceeds the knowledge of scholars, namely, informing of the unseen, and that he would inform them of the food that would be brought to them. He made that a transition to mentioning to them Tawhid, presenting faith to them, making it attractive to them, and making polytheism with Allah hateful to them. This is a method that every person of knowledge should follow with the ignorant and the sinful (p-3543) when one of them asks him for a ruling: he should first present guidance, direction, good admonition, and sincere advice, and call him to what is more fitting for him and more obligatory upon him than what he asked about, and then give him the ruling after that. And in it: when a scholar's rank in knowledge is unknown, and he describes himself with what he is qualified for, his aim being that knowledge be drawn from him and benefited from in religion, it is not a matter of self-praise. End quote.

After establishing the truth, calling them to it, and explaining to them his rank in knowledge, he began to interpret what they had asked about. And because this is a topic different from what preceded it, he separated it from that by repeating the address, and said:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[41] ﴿O two companions of the prison! As for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾

﴿O two companions of the prison! As for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink﴾ means: he will leave the prison and return to what he was before, giving his master (sayyid) wine to drink. ﴿But as for the other, he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head﴾ means: he will be killed and hung upon a wooden post, and birds will eat from the flesh of his head.

﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire﴾ means: what you both inquire about has been cut off and completed. That is, its outcome, which is the salvation of one of them and the destruction of the other. Its being expressed as "the matter" (al-amr), and the seeking of its interpretation as "inquiry" (al-istifta'), is to magnify its gravity and exalt its importance, since inquiry (al-istifta') occurs only in unprecedented incidents whose ruling is problematic and whose answer is unclear. The choice of the present-tense form (ṣighat al-istiqbal), despite their having already inquired about it, is because they were on the verge of it, until he, peace be upon him, should fulfill his need of the answer.

(p-3544) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[142] ﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord." But Satan caused him to forget the mention of his lord, so he remained in the prison for several years.﴾

﴿And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, "Mention me to your lord"﴾ That is: Yusuf said to the one whom he knew would be saved from the two young men, i.e., that he would be freed from prison and from execution, and he was the cupbearer: ﴿"Mention me to your lord"﴾, meaning, mention my condition and my attribute, and my knowledge of dream interpretation, and what has befallen me, to the king, your master, perhaps he will free me from that of which I have been wronged.

And (ẓann, "thought") is used in the sense of knowledge and certainty, and it occurs frequently, and expressing it this way is a loosening of the reins and a courtesy toward God, exalted is He. It has also been said: ẓann is in its well-known meaning, based on the fact that Yusuf's interpretation was by way of ijtihad (independent reasoning), and the judgment of a matter by its decree is also ijtihadi; but the first is more fitting to the context.

Note:

The verse indicates the permissibility of seeking help from one who is likely to relieve distress, even if he is a polytheist. This has come in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And cooperate in righteousness and piety﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2], and His words, relating about Jesus: ﴿Who are my helpers toward God?﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 52]. And in the hadith: "God is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother." It is evident that this is part of the order of existence and of human civilization, and for this reason man was distinguished by speech.

As for what Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Had he (meaning Yusuf) not said the word that he said, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did, since he sought relief from other than God, exalted is He." Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: "It is a very weak hadith," and he mentioned among its narrators two weak transmitters by name. Then he said: (p-3545) It is also narrated as a mursal (broken chain) from al-Hasan and Qatadah. He said: "These mursal reports are not accepted here, even if mursal reports were accepted in themselves in other contexts — and God knows best." He has done well and benefited, may Allah have mercy on him.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the mention of his lord﴾ mean: Satan occupied him until he forgot to mention Yusuf to the king. ﴿So he remained﴾, that is, Yusuf stayed ﴿in the prison for several years﴾, that is, a portion of them.

The lexicographers have various views on (bid') (a few, "several"): that it is between three and nine, or up to five, or what does not reach a decade nor half of it, meaning between one and four. Other views have also been given.

When relief drew near to Yusuf, peace be upon him, by God's mercy, through the means He had prepared, the Pharaoh of Egypt saw this dream, to which God alluded in His words:

The discussion of the Exalted's words:

[43] ﴿And the king said, "Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears [of grain] and others dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions."﴾

﴿And the king said﴾ i.e., to his chieftains: ﴿Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones﴾ i.e., perishing from emaciation. ʿIjāf is the plural of ʿajfāʾ, meaning the emaciated one, the opposite of the fat one. ﴿And seven ears [of grain]﴾ i.e., and I see a second vision: seven ears ﴿green and others dry﴾ i.e., and seven others, dry and thin, which sprouted behind them, and they swallowed up the green ears that were full. He omitted their number and the destruction of the green ones only because what was mentioned about the state of the cows suffices, since they are their counterpart.

And his words: ﴿O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions﴾ are an address to the nobles of his people. He had summoned, right after waking, the sorcerers and wise men of Egypt and recounted to them this vision of his.

(p-3546) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿They said, "These are confused dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."﴾

﴿They said﴾, that is, the chiefs (al-mala') said to the king. ﴿Confused dreams﴾, that is, their jumbled mixtures. It is the plural of (ḍighth) (a bundle), which originally means what is gathered from mixed herbs and tied together. It was then used figuratively for what the imaginative faculty (al-quwwa al-mutakhayyilah) gathers of the soul's inner talk (aḥādīth al-nafs) and the whisperings of Satan, and displays in sleep. And (al-aḥlām) is the plural of (ḥulm), which is what the sleeper sees. It is synonymous with (ru'yā) (vision), except that the latter has come to be used predominantly for good visions and fine things, while (ḥulm) has come to be used for the opposite. In a hadith: "The vision is from Allah, and the ḥulm is from Satan."

Al-Turbashti said: Among the Arabs, (ḥulm) is used in the same way as (ru'yā). The distinction is one of the terms established by the Lawgiver to separate truth from falsehood, as if he disliked calling what is from Allah and what is from Satan by one name. So he made (ru'yā) an expression for the good among them, because (ru'yā) implies seeing with the eye or the insight, and he made (ḥulm) an expression for what is from Satan, because the original sense of the word was used only for what is imagined to the dreamer in his sleep of fulfilling desire, which has no reality. End of quotation.

The plural in (al-aḥlām) is meant to refer to more than one, because they were two dreams, each of which one of them saw upon waking from it, as has been narrated. Some understood it to be a single dream and sought a reason for the plural, saying: either it is for emphasis in describing it as false, or because it includes various different things. There is no need for this, as we have explained.

﴿And we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams﴾ may mean that they intended by (dreams) only false dreams in particular, that is: there is no interpretation for them according to us, and interpretation pertains only to true visions. Or it may mean that they acknowledge the deficiency of their knowledge and that they are not experts in interpretation (ta'bīr).

Al-Nāṣir said: This is the apparent meaning. Taking the statement in the first sense makes it belong to the category of the line of verse:

"On a broad, trackless road whose landmarks cannot guide one"

(p-3547) As if they said: and there is no interpretation for false dreams, so that we would be knowledgeable about it. The king's earlier statement to them, ﴿If you are able to interpret dreams, [then explain]﴾ [Yusuf: 43], is evidence that they were not knowledgeable in his view about them, because he used the word of doubt, and their admission of deficiency corresponds to the king's doubt, which he put in the form of a question about whether they were knowledgeable about visions or not. And the youth's statement, ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ [Yusuf: 45] up to his words ﴿so that I may return to the people, that they may know﴾ [Yusuf: 46], is also evidence for that — and Allah knows best.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[45] ﴿And the one of the two who had been saved, and who remembered after a period of time, said: I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth.﴾

﴿And the one of the two who had been saved from them﴾ — i.e., from the two companions of the prison, and he was the cupbearer. ﴿And who remembered after a period of time﴾ — i.e., he recalled [Yusuf] after a span of time. His remembrance, according to what has been related, was after two years. ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ — i.e., I will inform you of it by receiving it from the one who has its knowledge, not from my own opinion. For this reason he did not say: "I will give you a fatwa concerning them." He followed this with His saying ﴿so send me forth﴾ — i.e., send me to Yusuf. He did not mention him [by name] only because of his confidence in what had preceded of the remembrance and what followed of his words.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted: [46] ﴿Yūsuf, O man of truth, give us your interpretation concerning seven fat cows which seven lean ones devour, and seven green ears of grain and others dry, that I may return to the people, so that they may know.﴾

﴿Yūsuf, O man of truth﴾ means: he sent to him, so he came to him and said, "Yūsuf!" He described him with exaggeration in truthfulness, according to what he had experienced of his circumstances and had come to know of his truthfulness in interpreting his dream and the dream of his companion, where it came to pass as he had interpreted. This was because he was about to seize the opportunity of his knowledge, so it belongs to the category of the excellent opening (barāʿat al-istihlāl). ﴿Give us your interpretation concerning seven fat cows which seven lean ones devour, and seven green ears of grain and others dry﴾ means: concerning the interpretation of that dream. He did not change the king's wording, because the interpretation follows its form, as they explained. In his saying ﴿give us﴾, although he was the one seeking the interpretation alone, there is an indication that the dream was not his own, but belonged to another who is involved in public affairs, and that he was in that matter an interpreter and an envoy, as his saying indicated: ﴿that I may return to the people﴾, meaning to the king and those around him, ﴿so that they may know﴾, meaning: that they may act in accordance with its requirement, or that they may know your merit and your standing in knowledge, so that they seek you out and free you from your ordeal. He did not state the matter definitively, but said "perhaps" (laʿallī) and "perhaps they" (laʿallahum) in accommodation to him, following the way of courtesy, and as a precaution against rashness, since he was not certain of returning, for perhaps death would overtake him before that.

*The poet said:*

"Perhaps the fates lie beyond what you count for me."

Nor [did he speak definitively] from their knowledge of that, for perhaps they did not know it. This was noted by Abū al-Suʿūd.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 12, verses 47–49**

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

[47] ﴿He said: "You will sow for seven years in succession. Whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears, except for a little of which you eat."﴾

[48] ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years, which will consume what you have stored up for them, except for a little of what you have kept aside.﴾ [Yusuf: 48]

[49] ﴿Then after that will come a year in which the people will be given rain, and in which they will press (juice).﴾ [Yusuf: 49]

﴿He said﴾, that is, Yusuf, in interpreting it: ﴿You will sow for seven years in succession﴾, that is, persistently and diligently, every year of them. ﴿Whatever you harvest﴾, that is, of the crop. ﴿Leave it in its ears﴾, that is, do not thresh it, for this keeps it better. ﴿Except for a little of which you eat﴾, that is, during those years, meaning in the amount you eat.

﴿Then after that﴾ [Yusuf: 48], that is, after the aforementioned seven years, ﴿will come seven hard years﴾ [Yusuf: 48], that is, seven years difficult for the people because of the severity of the famine. ﴿Which will consume what you have stored up for them﴾ [Yusuf: 48], that is, the grains you have set aside for them, left in their ears. Since he expressed the cows by "years," he attributed the eating to the years, just as he saw in the vision the cows eating, so that there is correspondence between the thing expressed, which is what was seen in the dream, and the thing by which it is expressed, which is its interpretation. The rational metaphor (al-majaz al-'aqli, a figurative attribution of an action to something other than its true agent), meaning "it is eaten in them," is not required, as in the phrase "his day is fasting," because it may be a case of mushakala (a figure of speech in which a word is used because of its association with another word in the same context) in that context. ﴿Except for a little of what you keep aside﴾ [Yusuf: 48], that is, what you guard and store up for sowing.

﴿Then after that﴾ [Yusuf: 48], that is, after the years described as hard, and the consumption of the stored grain, ﴿will come a year in which the people will be given rain﴾ [Yusuf: 49], that is, they will receive rain, or they will be relieved from the drought, or He will lift from them what they dislike through relief. ﴿And in which they will press (juice)﴾ [Yusuf: 49], that is, what they used to press according to their custom, such as grapes, olives, and the like.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The mention of "pressing" (al-'asr), although it could have been dispensed with by mentioning "rain," which normally entails it, just as he dispensed with mentioning their handling of the grains, is either because rain does not entail pressing in the same way that it entails grains, since the things mentioned depend for their good condition on other causes besides rain; or it is out of consideration for the one asking, taking into account his particular situation, as good news for him. This is the point on which the excellence of the placement of his (Yusuf's) inclusion among "the people" depends, in the reading with the second-person ta' (the reading in which the verb is addressed to the people, with the letter ta' placed above). It has been said that the meaning of "they press" is "they milk the udders." End of quote.

The wording, in its general meaning, includes this, because milking involves squeezing the udder so that the milk comes out.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The interpretation of the fat cows and the green ears is fertile years, and of the lean and dry ones is barren years. Then, after finishing the interpretation of the dream, he gave them the good news that the eighth year would come blessed, fertile, abundant in goodness and plentiful in blessings, and that this came by way of revelation.

**Note:**

Al-Iklil (The Crown) said: This verse is among the foundations of dream interpretation. It also shows that the dreams of unbelievers can be valid, that it is permissible to call him (the king) a "king," and that our saying "dreams belong to the first interpreter" is not a general rule for every dream. This is because they said: ﴿confused dreams﴾ [Yusuf: 44], and their saying this did not make the dream void. Thus the rule applies only to a dream that admits several possible meanings, one of which is interpreted and then comes to pass. In His words ﴿Then after that will come a year﴾ [Yusuf: 49], etc., there is an addition beyond what was asked about, from which it is inferred that there is no harm in doing this in both dream interpretation and giving religious rulings (fatwa). End of quote.
