Al-Isma'ili added from him: "They were human, weakened, despaired, and thought that they had been denied."

Al-Bukhari related that ʿAʾishah used to read (kadhdhabū) with a shadda and interpret it according to the first meaning. ʿUrwah said to her: "Perhaps it is (kadhabū) without the shadda." She said: "God forbid!"

Ibn Hajar said: This clearly shows that she rejected the reading without the shadda, and perhaps it had not reached her from those to whom one refers in that matter. It was read without the shadda by the imams of the Kufan readers: ʿAsim, Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i. Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Qaʿqaʿ agreed with them among the Hijazi readers. It is also the reading of Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, and others.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever We willed was saved﴾ refers to the messengers and the believers with them. It is also read (fa-nunjī) with lightening and with doubling, and it is read (fa-najā).

﴿But Our punishment is not averted﴾ meaning: Our chastisement. ﴿From the criminal people﴾ meaning: when it descends upon them.

In this there is an indication of those whom God willed to save, for from the contrast one knows that those who are not criminals are the ones who were saved, and they are the ones mentioned earlier.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 12, verse 111 (part 1 of 4):**

(p-3617) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:
[111] ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. It was not an invented narration, but a confirmation of what was before it, and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾

﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾ The pronoun refers either to Joseph and his brothers, or to the prophets and their nations. Al-Zamakhshari preferred the second view, based on the reading *qisasihim* with a kasra on the qaf, the plural of *qissa* (story). The version with a fatha is a verbal noun used in the sense of the object. It is answered that the story of Joseph, his father and his brothers contains various stories and accounts, and the plural may be used for the singular, as already mentioned in *"adghath ahlam"* (confused dreams). We will mention the aspects of the lessons drawn from them, with His help, Exalted is He.

﴿It was not...﴾ That is, the Qur'an, which is indicated by what precedes it with clear indication. ﴿an invented narration﴾ That is, something fabricated. ﴿but a confirmation of what was before it﴾ That is, of the revealed books. It confirms what in them is sound, and negates what has occurred in them of distortion, alteration and change, and it judges over them by abrogation (*naskh*, the cancellation of a earlier ruling by a later one) or by affirmation.

Some of the researchers said: what is meant is that the stories of the Qur'an are not invented or fabricated, as evidenced by the existence of their like among people before its revelation. Although they differ slightly in some details and particulars from what people narrate, they agree with them in general and confirm them in essence. So do not suppose, O polytheists, that the Prophet invented them by his own intellect. Rather, ask the People of the Book about them, and you will find that they are known among them and transmitted in their books. The existence of the Qur'an's stories among people beforehand is among the greatest things that confirm and support it, because the Prophet, may the blessings of God be upon him, had not looked into the books of the People of the Book. Do not imagine from this verse that the stories of the Qur'an must not differ from the stories of the Torah and the Gospel in anything at all. Certainly not, for if this were correct (p-3618) it would not have been said, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that about which they differ﴾ [al-Naml: 76]. Its stories may differ from what they have, and it clarifies for them what is true from what is false. There is therefore no contradiction between the Qur'an's confirmation of their stories in general and its disagreement with them in some particulars, as we have said. It is also possible that what is meant by His saying ﴿confirmation of what was before it﴾ is the confirmation of the truth that is with them, not all that is with them. Otherwise, their corrupt beliefs, their illusions, their superstitions and others, which the Qur'an came to remove and erase, would be included in that, and it would be impossible for it to confirm what came to nullify it. So reflect upon this, and do not be among the heedless. End.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ That is, a clarification of everything that is needed of the rulings of the lawful and the unlawful, of manners and morals, and of the aspects of lessons and admonitions. For this reason it is the greatest means by which hearts are rescued from error to right guidance, and from misguidance to rectitude, and by which mercy is sought from the Lord of the servants, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿and guidance﴾ That is, from misguidance, ﴿and mercy﴾ That is, from punishment, ﴿for a people who believe﴾ That is, who affirm it and act upon its commands, for faith is speech, conviction and action. He specified them because they are the ones who benefit from it.

**Conclusion on important matters**

The first: concerning what has been said about the aspects of lessons in this narrative.

In *al-Lubab* it is said: *i'tibar* (taking a lesson) and *ibra* (lesson) are the state by which a person reaches from knowledge of what is observed to what is not observed. What is meant by it is contemplation and reflection. The aspect of taking a lesson from this story is that the One who was able to bring Joseph out of the well after he had been thrown into it, and to bring him out of prison, and to give him dominion over Egypt after slavery, and to reunite him with his father and brothers after a long period and despair of reunion, is able to exalt Muhammad (ﷺ) and raise his word and manifest his religion. And the report of this wondrous story is like the report of unseen matters, so it was a miracle for him (ﷺ).

(p-3619) Some of them said: The story of Joseph the Truthful is abundant in benefit and noble in its return, and it urges every noble person to follow it. For whoever lets loose his thought upon the life of Joseph, peace be upon him, finds it comfortable and pleasant, and that is only because of the goodness of his conduct, the praiseworthiness of his inner nature, and his holding fast to the bonds of piety and virtue, especially the virtue of chastity and purity, which raises the rank of its possessor and places him in a lofty station. So a person should follow the trace of this noble virtue, as Joseph did, so that he ascends the summit of glory in this world and attains lasting happiness in the Hereafter. End.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: This surah is among what was related to the Prophet, may the blessings of God be upon him, of the reports of the messengers and the accounts of those who preceded him, which contains the firmness referred to in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We relate to you all [the news of the messengers]﴾ [Hud: 120], and so on. It was singled out on its own and was not coupled with the stories of the messengers, although they are in one surah, because its content is different from those stories. Do you not see that those stories concern the sending of the messengers mentioned before them, peace be upon them, the manner in which their peoples received them, and the destruction of those who denied them? As for this story, its outcome is: relief after hardship, and an indication of the good end of patience. God tested Jacob, peace be upon him, with the loss of his two sons and his sight, and the dispersal of his children. He tested Joseph, peace be upon him, with the well, the sale, the wife of the chief, the loss of his father and brothers, and prison. Then He tested them all with the widespread harm and the scarcity of means: ﴿Harm has touched us and our family﴾ [Yusuf: 88], and so on. Then God made it up to them by reuniting them with one another, gathering their scattered order, restoring their father's sight, harmonizing their hearts, removing what Satan had stirred up, rescuing Joseph, peace be upon him, despite the plotting of those who plotted against him, surrounding him with protection, and clearing his name before the king and the women. All of this resulted from beautiful patience, the sublimity of certainty, and the good acceptance of destinies through entrusting and submission, through successive trials and a long period. Then, in the course of this noble story, the repentance of the wife of the chief came, and her return to the truth, and her testimony for Joseph, peace be upon him, to what God had granted him of purity from everything that stains. Then the chief's choosing him for himself, along with what (p-3620) was linked in this noble story of wonders and lessons. This story stood alone and did not match the stories mentioned of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, Shu'ayb and Moses, peace be upon them, and what took place among their peoples. Therefore it was separated from them. In a separate surah He alluded to the end of one who is patient, content and submissive, so that the believers would be alerted to what is contained within that. And what this surah had summarized of the allusion was explicitly stated in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession in the earth﴾ [al-Nur: 55], up to His saying: ﴿security﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. The story of Joseph, peace be upon him, in its entirety was most similar to the condition of the believers in their struggle at the beginning, their emigration, their division from their people, and their scarcity of means, until God gathered their scattered order: ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you, when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so by His favour you became brothers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 103]. He made them inherit the earth, supported them and gave them victory, and that was because of their magnificent faith and their great patience. This is what necessitated the singling out of this story from those stories, and God knows best.

Then, the condition of Jacob and Joseph, peace be upon them both, in their patience, and in seeing the good end of patience in this world, and what was prepared for them of great reward, is most fitting for the condition of our Prophet, peace be upon him, in his struggle with Quraysh, his departure from his homeland, and then the sequel to that with his triumph over his enemy, the strengthening of his religion, the manifestation of his word, and his return to his land, in a state that gladdened the eyes of the believers, and what God opened for him and his companions. So reflect upon this! What clarifies it is the closing of the surah with His saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ [Yusuf: 110], and so on. The essence of all this is the command to patience and the good end of God's friends through it. Thus [it is stated] in the *Tafsir al-Burhan* of al-Biqa'i, summarized. 

In the book *al-Nizam wal-Islam*, in the section on education and manners in the stories of the Qur'an, there came the following example:

The matter has been long for our nation, so it neglected what lies within the pages of its book of the foundation of education and wisdom, and how capable men are selected for the important tasks. Would that I knew! What has befallen it, that it turned away from the stories that the Qur'an related, neglected their matter, and its people thought they were merely historical matters that benefit only (p-3621) historians? The stories in every nation are the basis of its advancement, whether they are fabricated or real, told through the tongues of animals, humans or inanimate things. On this, nations, old and new, have reflected. Consider the book *Kalila wa Dimna* and the stories that followed its pattern in Islam, such as the book *Fakihat al-Khulafa'* and the *Maqamat* of al-Hariri. The Qur'an came with the stories of the prophets, and they are, beyond doubt, higher in attainment and nobler in distinction. How could they not be, since they combine the finest style, the selection of the settings suited to what they were brought for, the good example for the perfect sincere ones among the prophets and those who follow them, and their realization in themselves, because of the occurrence of their sources. The love of imitation is a disposition rooted in man, especially for one who follows them. These are five advantages that these stories have been singled out with, and which others lack. Is it not a manifest shame that we read the stories of the Qur'an and hardly understand anything but narratives that have passed with time, and gone by like yesterday's past? What have we to do with them? By God, this is indeed ruin! This was only because of ignorance of the purpose of its stories. They are a lesson for whoever takes lessons, a reminder for whoever reflects, and an insight for whoever is restrained. As for returning to history and comparing it with what the historians related in their books, and what the ancients wrote in contradiction to them, and what the storytellers say in their fables, that is the path of one who deviates from the highway, in which the skilled go astray. What guides you to this is what you hear of the account of the People of the Cave, and how He says: ﴿They will say: they were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say: five, the sixth of them being their dog, guessing at the unseen; and they will say: seven, and the eighth of them being their dog. Say: My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few﴾ [al-Kahf: 22]. Observe how He attributed knowledge to God, and did not rely on the saying of the disputing historians, and then did not state the reality, lest it become a pretext for attacking the revelation. If one says five, they say six; if one says four, they say seven. The books of historians are very much in disagreement about the stories, and their purpose is only that they be a lesson. In sum, the aim of these stories is nothing but their benefits, and the illuminating lessons for the listeners: ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾

[p-3622] We are not among those who boast of speech without proof, so we rely only on demonstration. Reflect on these stories, and you will find that they mention only what suits guidance and counsel, and they pass over many events that have no necessity and no reliance upon them. Every story contains tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), knowledge, noble character, rational arguments, insight and remembrance, and beautiful dialogues that delight the intelligent. I will limit myself among these stories to what he related about Yusuf the Truthful, peace be upon him, and how he went beyond everything unrelated to character, such as the civic life and conditions of the Egyptians, to the essence and the fruit. Do you not see how it began with the account of the sun, the moon and the stars prostrating to him in a dream? This indicates that a child has a disposition (isti'dad) that appears in his features, his sayings, his actions and his dreams. This is the greatest thing that the ancient sages, from the Greeks and the Persians, were concerned with, as the historians and scholars of ethics have mentioned. They used to test their sons and examine their features, so that they might know for what crafts, leaderships and sciences they were prepared.

Then reflect on the story of the brothers, the shirt, the well, the wolf and the blood, so that you may know what we witness every day of rivalry of peers against one in whom the marks of inner beauty, good character and outward majesty have appeared. They find fault with him in what harms his self, his honor or his character. This indicates that this is a sunnah (established pattern) in the universe that does not spare a prophet, a sage or a scholar, however good his character and however beautiful his outward and inner being may be......!

 *Every enmity may hopefully be removed, except the enmity of one who opposes you out of envy.*

This sunnah operates among people: if the righteous person endures patiently, he attains authority over them, and they come to love him after enmity, even if after some time, and they turn against whoever harmed him! Then consider the story of the wife of the Governor, and how he kept chaste in youth, how he governed his own self, how the trust of his master in his honesty proved right, how he pleased his Lord, and how he was marked by virtue, so that his inner and outer beauty were balanced..! Let us stop at this point now, and begin speaking about the manners, the ethics, the training of rulers, and the pardon and forgiveness contained in that story!

As for the science of ethics and the training of the heads of nations from it, reflect on the words of the sages, the first and the last of them, (p-3623) and you will find their consensus that the governance of the character of the self comes first, then the household, then the city. Each one is a prerequisite for the next and a fruit of the one before it, for it is not conceivable that one who has not governed himself should govern his household, or that one who has not managed his household should govern his community!

The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, gave the pledge to the first Caliph. He took cloth and a measuring rod and went to the market in the morning. The Companions were displeased and blamed him. He said: "If I neglect my family, I will be even more negligent toward the Muslims!" So they assigned him a stipend from the public treasury (bayt al-mal), and he said: "In that case I will look into your affairs!" Therefore, we find that Westerners, when they appoint a man to manage their country, ask extensively about his spouse and the management of his household, knowing that his household is closer to him than the nation is.

So look at these truths from the biography of the Prophet Yusuf the Truthful: how they are mentioned in the Heavenly Books and arranged in the Qur'an in a firm order. In it the three policies are mentioned in this order: self, then household, then city, a natural arrangement, as an alert to the sons of Islam to know this science and to choose the capable for public affairs. Thus it points to the training of noble character through chastity in the bloom of youth, along with truthfulness. How could he preserve the character of his fathers, his people and the prophets amid the civilization of the Egyptians, its ornaments and its beauty, worship God alone, and forget what he saw of the Sphinx (Abu al-Hawl), Apis, and the scattered deities....?! This recounts an insight for those surrounded by the waves of events from every side: that they should preserve the roots and principles of their religion, and then do whatever they wish in the affairs of their worldly life..!

The truthfulness of Yusuf appeared in his personal character, but that alone was not sufficient for managing his public affairs. So he was placed in prison and surrounded by youths and ignorant people from every side. He began to govern them as a man governs the people of his household, and he spread his creed among them, showing himself in the guise of perfection, kindness and compassion toward them: ﴿He said: No food will come to you that you are provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it reaches you﴾ [Yusuf: 37], and so on. He began to relate to them the biography of his ancestors, his love for their creed, and his hatred for the idols of the Egyptians and the like. He said: ﴿Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 37], and so on. Then he began to remind them that the scattering of a nation's direction is misguidance in politics, and that unifying its direction is wisdom in it. He said: ﴿O my two companions in prison, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39]. Thus scattering of direction is the dispersal of the community. No nation has ever prospered in existence except through men who unify its direction, whatever it may be, so that they aim at one goal! The details are not hidden from people of understanding..!

In "The Opinions of the People of the Virtuous City" (Ara' Ahl al-Madina al-Fadila) by al-Farabi, there are twelve unifying bonds, each of which is a people united by it: such as language, homeland, religion, ethics, lineage, the wise guide, the great father, and similar things by which a nation or community is distinguished.

When both matters were completed for him, peace be upon him, namely the governance of the self and of the clan, he was brought out of prison, honored and esteemed. He advanced from teaching the destitute in prison to teaching kings on their thrones. He began to train them on how to economize wealth, interpreted for them the green ears and the dry ones, and the fat cows and the lean ones, and guided them to storing grain with its ears so that it would not spoil, and other public affairs. This is the third stage: governing the whole nation after crossing those two obstacles.

Skill and shrewdness in the sciences of civilization and in managing the affairs of the nation come either through revelation, which is specific to him and to prophets like him, peace be upon them, or through instruction and training, which is fitting for all other people.

This noble biography guides to the fact that noble character is that which the soul remains steadfast in, with the lowly and the great, the small and the large, and that a person should not disdain teaching the young, for he will inevitably one day reach the great, as in the hadith of Heraclius with Abu Sufyan, and the teaching of the Truthful one to those in prison. Thus the companion of the prison conveyed to the Pharaoh of the Egyptians.

(p-3625) This Prophet was tested with ease and hardship, yet his character did not change. He was the model of perfection in the expanse of the house of kingship and majesty, and the locus of trust in the narrowness of the prison's grave and the ten lowly circumstances through which character changes, the roots of lineage are forgotten, and the perfect person is brought down from the thrones of virtue to the lowest seats of vice, and from the peak of perfection to the depths of deficiency!

This is the story of Yusuf, who was raised in Egypt and grew up there, and whom the ornaments of that civilization did not lure into vice. It came as a lesson for all people and especially for the Egyptians! By these characteristics Yusuf ascended the throne of greatness and majesty. He governed Egypt after having been governed, and he ruled after having been a slave! Recompense for character and perfection is not reserved for the Hereafter only, but occurs in both abodes: ﴿And thus We established Yusuf in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. We give mercy to whom We will, and We do not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾ [Yusuf: 56]. ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 57].

These are the virtuous characteristics, mentioned in the revelation as a model within the course of this biography, for the Islamic nations, so that they may take its fruit and not waste time on its origin and source in history, just as the exegete stagnates over grammatical parsing, morphology or rhetoric. This is a drop from an ocean of the wisdoms of this story, and through it we understand what was mentioned at its beginning: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories by what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an﴾ [Yusuf: 3]. Leave aside the speech of the ignorant, the understanding of the ascetics, and the confusion and disagreement of the historians, and listen to what this story contains of the arrangement for training rulers and governors, as we pointed out earlier, and let us add further clarification!

The scholars of ethics and the sages have said: the affairs of a nation are not ordered except by reformers, capable men of action, and virtuous guides who give direction, who have known conditions and recognized characteristics. If the one who undertakes the affairs is a prophet, he has forty qualities that they have enumerated, all of which are manners and virtues by which he governs his nation. If he is a virtuous ruler of a virtuous city, they are content with some of the forty conditions. Our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, possessed the perfection of the messengers and the beauty of the prophets. There came in his biography what intelligent nations take as guidance for choosing the capable for great tasks, since he possessed both kingship and prophethood! We have no capacity for prophethood, since it has ended, and we only mention what befits the station of the head of a virtuous city. We will mention from them thirteen qualities, which are the most important characteristics of the head of a virtuous city, so that they may serve as a reminder for those who reflect on the Qur'an, and as an alert for learners who love virtues to the precious treasures of the Great Book, and to encourage them to look into the Qur'an, and so that they may know that these stories contain what never would have occurred to the mind of one who heard them merely for entertainment, singing, and mere amusement and play!

The most important conditions that the sages stipulated for the head of the virtuous city:

1. Chastity from desires, so that he controls his self and his psychic strength is complete: ﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants﴾ [Yusuf: 24].

2. Forbearance at the time of anger, so that he controls his self: ﴿They said: If he steals, there had already stolen a brother of his before. But Yusuf concealed it within himself and did not reveal it to them﴾ [Yusuf: 77].

3. Placing gentleness in its place and firmness in its place: ﴿And when he had supplied them with their supplies, he said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts? But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, nor shall you approach me﴾ [Yusuf: 59-60]. The first part is for gentleness and the latter for firmness.

4. Self-confidence: ﴿Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I am a knowing guardian﴾ [Yusuf: 55].

5. Strength of memory, so that he can recall what was absent and what years have passed, in order to govern affairs and to recognize people's deeds: ﴿And the brothers of Yusuf came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him﴾ [Yusuf: 58].

(p-3627) 6. Excellence of imagination and the imaginative faculty, until it brings things in complete clarity: ﴿Indeed, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me﴾ [Yusuf: 4].

7. His readiness for knowledge, his love for it, and his mastery of it: ﴿And I follow the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ [Yusuf: 38]. ﴿And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge; and thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [Yusuf: 22]. ﴿My Lord, You have given me of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾ [Yusuf: 101].

8. His compassion toward the weak and his humility despite the greatness of his rank and the height of his position. He addressed the two imprisoned youths with humility, saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison﴾ [Yusuf: 39], and so on, and he conversed with them about the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. To the first he said: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ [Yusuf: 37]; and to the second: ﴿Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 37], and so on. And they both bore witness to him by their words: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good﴾ [Yusuf: 36].

9. Forgiveness while having power: ﴿He said: No reproach will there be upon you today. May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ [Yusuf: 92].

10. Honoring one's kin: ﴿And bring me your family, all of them﴾ [Yusuf: 93].

The strength of eloquence and expression in his interpreting of the king's dream, and his capacity to win over hearts, from the shepherd to the subject and the common folk. This was achieved only through eloquence founded on knowledge and wisdom: ﴿So when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, today you are with us established and trusted."﴾ [Yusuf: 54]

12. Excellence of management: ﴿Whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears of grain.﴾ [Yusuf: 47] and so on.

Then consider Yusuf's (peace be upon him) capacity to govern the king's affairs, and how he drew hearts to himself through kindness: ﴿And he said to his servants, "Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags."﴾ [Yusuf: 62] and so on. He devised the wondrous stratagem of the matter of the drinking cup and the accusation of theft, so that he might take his brother to himself: ﴿So he began with their bags﴾ [Yusuf: 76] and so on. He dealt with those under his rule according to their law, their religion, their creed and their customs, as is the practice of all the living Eastern nations, in showing gentleness to the ruled nation. They govern them according to their religion, their customs, their law, their morals and their property, following what the glorious Shari'a has laid down that suits the judgment of our master Yusuf (peace be upon him). For he commanded his followers to ask them: ﴿They said, "The penalty for it, if you are lying, is ..."﴾ [Yusuf: 74] and so on. The law of the children of Ya'qub was that the thief be enslaved for a year to the owner of the property, so he dealt with them according to what they held. For this reason God Most High says: ﴿He could not have taken his brother under the king's law, except that God willed it. We raise in degrees whomever We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.﴾ [Yusuf: 76] He was praised for the excellence of his plan in governance and for his observance of the custom of those people. Although this matter appears simple on the surface, it is the mother of politics and the foundation of the sciences of civilization ('umran), and the first thing that politicians and wise men are advised to do!

By Allah! How beautiful is the Qur'an, and how delightful is knowledge! I wonder how God can say after this: ﴿We raise in degrees whomever We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.﴾ [Yusuf: 76] Had it not been for the noble principle and the lofty wisdoms within it, together with its clarity and simplicity, for those of shallow views and dull heedlessness, it would not have given it this majesty and grandeur, and it would not have praised knowledge! So may God give life to knowledge and perpetuate its dominion!

It is also strange and wondrous that this stratagem involved concealing the drinking cup, and then he searched all their baggage: ﴿So he began with their bags before the bag of his brother, then he extracted it from his brother's bag.﴾ [Yusuf: 76] By Allah, this is precisely what all the kings of the earth do today, with their policies and their subtle handling of hidden affairs, and their dressing of these in various garments for the governing of their lands, seeking the attainment of beneficial aims, and entering houses through their doors. But between them and this Prophet lies a vast gulf...! Observe how this story gives these wondrous matters!

By my life! Whoever studies with care what we have dictated about this story will, when reciting it, imagine that he is witnessing the deeds of the present and past nations, as though he had studied the opinions of the people of the virtuous city (al-madina al-fadila), the customs of the wise and the politicians of nations, and witnessed the beauty of knowledge, literature, wisdom and good admonition, until he knows with certainty how God said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories, in that We have revealed to you this Qur'an, though before it you were certainly among the unaware.﴾ [Yusuf: 3] And He says at its end: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you.﴾ [Yusuf: 102] And He says: ﴿Say, "This is my way: I invite to God with insight, I and whoever follows me. And glory be to God; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."﴾ [Yusuf: 108] Then He mentioned that a person should not despair of the mercy of God, so He said: ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired...﴾ [Yusuf: 110] and so on. He then indicated that the aim is the lessons and reflection on the effect of stories and their fruits, not merely their explanation, for mere explanation is a simple matter that satisfies the simple-minded. Rather the aim is admonition and taking heed, so He said: ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for people of understanding. It was not a narration invented...﴾ [Yusuf: 111] and so on. This guides you, if you are of lofty resolve, to restrain yourself with those who study for a long time, and not to hasten toward leadership until the Book reaches its term, and until you attain a generous share of morals and sciences. There is no harm in holding offices and benefiting the community, provided one persists in devotion to knowledge and seeking more of it! This Prophet (peace be upon him) was patient for days upon days, and clothed himself in the vicissitudes of events, garment upon garment, until, when despair overcame, relief and elevation came!

Reflect! How this surah is read by its reciters, and heard by the ignorant who turn away from its signs! When they hear a beautiful voice, they think that this is the beauty of the Qur'an, and they say to the reciter, "Glory be to Him who gave you!" They rejoice in what they possess of knowledge of the outward forms and the splendour of recitation, or merely of explanation and knowledge of the story, and they do not look at the wisdoms deposited within it! How evil is ignorance! It leaves a man blind even if he wears fine robes and dresses in garments of false pottery and deceptive mirage... How many signs and lessons does man have in the heavens and the earth, yet he turns away from them! Sight, hearing and intellect were created for us so that we might look at what is in the heavens and the earth, of what the Originator created in the cosmos, and recite the Qur'an, which is the speech of the Originator of the cosmos, and that we might refine the depiction of meanings and clothe them in the most beautiful garment. Yet the intelligent turn away, let alone the common folk! Why do the common people not learn? Why do those of insight not advise and clarify? Why do people hardly understand?

We have mentioned a model of this surah to stir up the resolve of the intelligent, and to urge those who have sharpness, perceptiveness and sound intellects to return to their Book and reflect upon it, and to remove the doubts of those who have doubted these stories and turned away! It is evident that all the stories of the Qur'an are full of wisdoms like this story, and each one contains what the others do not, as though they were fruits of differing colours! Where is the one who comprehends this, among those who stop at its words while turning away from its signs? There is no wonder in this, for the souls of the base take wisdom and bring it down from the horizon of its heaven to the earth of their lowliness, just as water becomes bitter in the colocynth tree. So one of them seeks it for melodies, another for a simple story, another for amusement and passing time, and another stops at the words and their i'rab (grammatical parsing), their sarf (morphology) and their balagha (eloquence).

(p-3631) But this is loftier than what came before it, for it has traversed the path that is the words; yet it is far-fetched that one should reach the aim and the fruits unless he prepares those rules as an introduction to the aim and investigates it! Others hear the verses and then present them to history, while historians differ, as we have mentioned earlier. The likeness of these people in their course is only the likeness of a man who was given a steam engine to irrigate his field from the river. He sat beside it, abandoned its use, and began to reflect: From where does this iron come? Why does it draw water? To what height does it rise, and what is its cause? From where does the coal come, and by what routes does it travel until it reaches us? A month and two months pass, his crop wilts and his land is ruined! That is the likeness of one who reads the Qur'an and makes most of his concern its application to the words of historians, or the rules of the grammarians, or the morphologists, or the scholars of eloquence, and nothing more! Except a small portion for understanding! By Allah, this is an upending of the head, and taking the means as the end, like the one who wanted to perform Hajj but devoted his resolve to preparing provisions for years, then death seized him and he departed this life without having performed Hajj! That is their likeness...! End.

Section Two:

Those who permit sin upon the prophets, namely the Karramiyya and al-Baqillani, argued from what occurred from the brothers of Yusuf: their selling of their brother and their lying to their father, and from what occurred from Yusuf himself: his taking of his brother and his causing his father distress.

Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him, said in (al-Milal wa al-Nihal):

What they have argued with has no proof in it, because the brothers of Yusuf (peace be upon him) were not prophets, and no text has ever come, regarding their being prophets, not from the Qur'an, nor from an authentic Sunna, nor from consensus, nor from the statement of any of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them)! As for Yusuf (peace be upon him), he was a messenger of God by the explicit text of the Qur'an. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And Yusuf had certainly come to you before with clear evidences, but you remained in doubt about what he had brought you, until, when he died, you said, "Allah will never send after him a messenger."﴾ [Ghafir: 34] up to His saying: ﴿after him a messenger﴾ [Ghafir: 34]. As for his brothers, their actions testify that they were not scrupulous about great sins, so how could they be prophets?! But the two messengers, their father and their brother, asked forgiveness for them and dropped reproach from them!

The proof of what we have mentioned, that the claim that they were prophets is false, is the saying of God Most High, relating from their brother the messenger that he said to them: ﴿You are worse in position﴾ [Yusuf: 77]. It is absolutely impermissible that he should say this to a prophet of the prophets, indeed nor to righteous people! For honouring the prophets is obligatory upon all people, and righteous people are not worse in position. Indeed the son of Noah disobeyed his father more than the brothers of Yusuf disobeyed their father, yet the brothers of Yusuf did not disbelieve. It is not permissible for a Muslim to count among the prophets anyone for whom no text, consensus, or transmission universally accepted establishes the validity of his prophethood! There is no difference between affirming the prophethood of one who is not a prophet and denying the prophethood of one among them whose prophethood is valid! If they cite in this regard what was narrated from one of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, namely Zayd ibn Arqam: "Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), died only because there is no prophet after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the children of prophets are prophets!" then this is great heedlessness and the slip of a scholar, for several reasons:

The first: it is a claim for which there is no proof of its validity!

The second: if what was mentioned were true, it would be possible for Ibrahim to have been made a prophet in the cradle, as Jesus (peace be upon him) was, and as Yahya was given judgment as a child; according to this view, perhaps Ibrahim was a prophet, though he lived two years less two months, and far be it from God that this be so...!

The third: the son of Noah was a disbeliever by the explicit text of the Qur'an: he did other than righteous deeds. So if the children of prophets were prophets, this disbelieving son, who was displeased with, would have been a prophet. Far be it from God that this be so...!

The fourth: if that were so, it would necessarily follow that all the Jews would be prophets until today, indeed all the people of the earth would be prophets; for it would entail that all of Adam's biological offspring are prophets, since their father is a prophet, and the children of their children are prophets, since their fathers are prophets and they are the children of prophets, and so on, endlessly, until the matter reaches us! In this there is, for one upon whom the proof has been established and who persists in it, a disbelief that is not hidden. And success is from God!

Then Ibn Hazm said:

They also mentioned, meaning the Karramiyya and those who agree with them, the taking of his brother by Yusuf (peace be upon him), and his causing his father (peace be upon him) distress from him, and that he remained for a period during which he could have informed his father of his news, while knowing what the father suffered of grief over him, yet he did not do so, and there was between him and his father only ten nights! And by placing the king's drinking cup in his brother's bag, while all his other brothers did not know of this; then he ordered the one who called out: ﴿O caravan, you are indeed thieves!﴾ [Yusuf: 70] while they had stolen nothing. And God Most High says: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 24]; and his service to Pharaoh; and his saying to the one who was with him in prison: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ [Yusuf: 42].

Ibn Hazm said: All of this gives them no proof whatsoever. We will explain this, by Allah's power and strength, and in Allah the Exalted we seek support. As for his taking his brother and causing his father distress, there is no doubt that this was so that he would be gentle with his brother and so that his brothers would return to him. Had they taken his brother away, they might not have come back to him, since they would be in another kingdom where Yusuf, peace be upon him, had no authority and the king of Egypt had no authority there. And it was a means of bringing him together with them and uniting all of them! There is no reason to suspect the Messenger of Allah Yusuf, peace be upon him, who was given knowledge and understanding of interpretation, of anything except the best interpretation. Those who oppose us have no text contrary to what we have mentioned. It is not permissible to suspect a virtuous Muslim of disobeying his father, so how could it be suspected of the Messenger of Allah, may the blessings of Allah be upon him?!

As for their claim that he remained for a period during which he could have informed his father of his condition but did not, this is an extreme ignorance on the part of whoever claims it. Ya'qub was in the land of Kan'an, in the territory of Palestine, among a people who were nomadic and poor, speaking a different language, following a different obedience and a different religion, and belonging to a different nation! So Yusuf, peace be upon him, had no knowledge, after his separation from his father, of what he had done, nor whether he was alive or dead, beyond Allah the Exalted's promise that He would inform them of their deed against him. Nor did he find anyone he trusted whom he could send to him, because of the disagreement we have mentioned. Only someone who sees the lands of al-Sham and Egypt as under one ruler, one religion, one language and one nation, with the roads open, merchants coming and going, caravans moving out and returning, and the postal relays (barid) departing and arriving, would find this easy to assume. He would think that every white thing is fat, though the matter was not like that at that time, but was as we have stated before. The evidence for this is that when it became possible for him, he did not delay, and he summoned his father and all his family when people were in dire need of him and submitted to him because of the hunger that had spread over the land, and because of their privileged position with him. He waited for the promise of his Lord the Exalted, which He had made to him when they threw him into the well, and they came to him humbled and seeking, just as Allah the Exalted had promised him in his vision before they came to him.

As for Yusuf's words to his brothers: ﴿Indeed, you are thieves﴾ [Yusuf: 70], although they had not stolen the cup, but rather he himself had placed it in his brother's bag without them knowing: he, peace be upon him, spoke the truth, because they had stolen him from their father and sold him. He, peace be upon him, did not say, "You have stolen the cup." He only said: ﴿We miss the cup of the king﴾ [Yusuf: 72], and in that he was truthful, because he was not finding it, so he was indeed missing it, without doubt! As for his, peace be upon him, service to Pharaoh, he served him out of taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), and in a matter of right, in order that Allah the Exalted might rescue through his good management. Perhaps the king, or some of his close associates, had believed in him. Nonetheless, his service to him was, in every case, good and an act of virtue, and through it he reached reunion with his father, justice, and the preservation of lives, since he could not overpower him by force, and no other course was open to him. There is no doubt that this was permissible in the shari'ah (divine law) of Yusuf, peace be upon him, unlike our shari'ah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

As for the prostration of his parents, it was not forbidden in their law; rather it was a good act, and the realization of his true vision from Allah the Exalted. Perhaps that prostration was a greeting, like the prostration of the angels to Adam, peace be upon him. However, what is beyond doubt is that it was not a prostration of worship or of abasement, but only a prostration of honour, without any doubt.

As for his, peace be upon him, saying to the one who was with him in prison: ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ [Yusuf: 42], we do not know that the desire to be released from prison is forbidden to anyone. There is no evidence in his saying that he neglected calling to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but he encouraged this man who was with him in prison to do good and urged him to it! This is an obligation from two aspects: the first is the obligation to strive to remove injustice from him; the second is his calling to goodness and good deeds.

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord﴾ [Yusuf: 42], the pronoun in (ansahu, "caused him to forget"), which is the (ha'), refers to the young man who was with him in prison. That is: Satan caused him to forget to remind his lord about Yusuf's matter, peace be upon him. It is also possible that Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, and had he remembered Allah the Mighty and Majestic, he would have mentioned Yusuf's need, peace be upon him. The proof of this is the Mighty and Majestic's words: ﴿And he remembered after a period [of time]﴾ [Yusuf: 45]. So it is certainly established that the one who remembered after a period was the one whom Satan had caused to forget the remembrance of his lord until he remembered. Even if it were correct that the pronoun in (ansahu) refers to Yusuf, peace be upon him, there would be no deficiency or sin in that, since forgetting is not unlikely for the prophets!

As for His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 24], it is not as those who did not reflect carefully supposed, to the extent that some of the later scholars said: "He sat between her legs as a man sits with a woman." Far be it from Allah that such a thing should be attributed to a man among the righteous Muslims or their concealed ones! How then could it be attributed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?!

If it is said: this has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, through a chain of narration (isnad) that is sound, we say: yes! But no one's statement is a proof except what is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone! The error in that report is, without doubt, from those below Ibn 'Abbas, or perhaps Ibn 'Abbas did not affirm it with certainty, since he took it from someone unknown. Without doubt, it is something he heard and then mentioned, because he, may Allah be pleased with him, was not present at that and did not report it from the Messenger of Allah. It is impossible that Ibn 'Abbas would assert with certainty what he has no knowledge of!

But the meaning of the verse does not go beyond one of two aspects. Either he intended to fall upon her and strike her, as the Exalted said: ﴿And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾ [Ghafir: 5], and as one says: "I was about to do such-and-such to you," but he, peace be upon him, refrained from that because of a proof Allah showed him, by which he was sufficed from striking her, and he knew that fleeing was more beneficial to him and clearer for his innocence, as became evident afterwards from the judgement of the witness concerning the matter of the torn shirt. The second aspect: the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾ [Yusuf: 24], then the Exalted began another statement, saying: ﴿And he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. This is the apparent meaning of the verse without forced interpretation, and this is what we hold. The proof of his Lord here is prophethood and Allah the Mighty and Majestic's protection of him. Had it not been for the proof, he would have been inclined toward immorality, and this is beyond doubt! Perhaps whoever attributes this to the holy prophet Yusuf will exalt himself above such a vile position and be ruined. The Prophet ﷺ feared destruction for those who thought that suspicion about him when he said to the two Ansari men who met him: "This is Safiyyah." It is false and impossible for anyone to suppose that Yusuf, peace be upon him, was about to commit fornication while hearing the Exalted's words: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. So we ask those who oppose us about the intention to commit fornication: is it an evil or not an evil? It must be an evil. If one were to say it is not an evil, he would be opposing the consensus (ijma'). Since it is an evil, and He turned evil away from him, He has certainly turned away the intention from him! Moreover, she said: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil against your wife?﴾ [Yusuf: 25], and he denied that, so the truthful one who confirms the truth bore witness: "If his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful" [Yusuf: 26]. So it is established by the explicit text of the Qur'an that she lied, and since she lied by the explicit text of the Qur'an, he never intended evil against her, and so he never intended fornication at all. Had he intended fornication with her, he would have been among the truthful, and this is very clear! Likewise is the Exalted's statement about him that he said: ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plotting, I would incline toward them and be among the ignorant﴾ [Yusuf: 33], ﴿So his Lord responded to him and turned away from him their plotting﴾ [Yusuf: 34]. Thus it is established about him that he never inclined toward her.

The words of Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him, end here. I have quoted his words in full, because, as it is said:

"Not all beauty is entirely beautiful...!"
